title: Motion design that respects reduced motion
when: The user wants animations or transitions (reveals, fades, sliding panels) and they must stay comfortable for everyone.
prompt:
Goal: Purposeful motion with set durations and easings, plus a reduced motion path that removes movement but keeps feedback.
Steps:
1. Give every animation a job: show where something came from, confirm an action, or draw attention once. Drop the rest.
2. Tokens: --dur-fast 120ms (hover, press), --dur-base 200ms (menus), --dur-slow 320ms (panels); --ease-out cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) for entering.
3. Animate only transform and opacity; width, height, top and box-shadow force layout or paint work.
4. Make movement opt in: put slides and reveals inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), and under reduce use a plain fade or none.
5. In scripts check matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches before scroll, canvas or parallax effects.
6. Never flash more than 3 times per second; anything looping over 5 seconds needs a pause control.
Quality bar:
- Durations between 100 and 400 ms.
- Nothing moves on load unless it explains the layout.
- With reduced motion, state changes stay visible.
Pitfalls:
- Parallax and zoom effects that trigger vestibular symptoms.
- scroll-behavior: smooth with no reduced override.
- Animating layout properties.
Verify:
- [ ] A prefers-reduced-motion rule exists.
- [ ] Only transform and opacity animate.
- [ ] Durations use tokens.
- [ ] Long loops have a pause control.
Output: Motion tokens and rules in style.css, and a matchMedia guard in any animating script.

examples.input: quero animacoes suaves quando as secoes aparecem
examples.output: fade and 16px rise at 320ms inside no-preference, plain opacity under reduce, tokens on :root
